## Function Archive Run

Writes .morph/runs/<runId>/{deck.json, report.json, answers/} and commits them with Morph-Run trailers; append-only.

Behaviour: archiveRun(root, {runId, deck, report, answers?}, env): runId must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$, else {ok: false, error: "invalid runId: <runId>"}; an answer whose request.customId does not match it → {ok: false, error: "invalid answer id: <customId>"} (the first such, in order). dir = ".morph/runs/<runId>"; an existing root/dir → {ok: false, error: "archive <dir> already exists"} (a run id names one run forever). A refusal writes nothing. Else mkdir -p, write <dir>/deck.json = JSON.stringify(deck.cards, null, 2) + "\n" (the Deck File form, a JSON array of cards) and <dir>/report.json = JSON.stringify(report, null, 2) + "\n", then per answer in order <dir>/answers/<customId>.request.json = JSON.stringify(request, null, 2) + "\n" and, when text is not null, <dir>/answers/<customId>.answer.txt = text exactly; answers absent or [] → no answers/ directory. Then Commit Paths over [<dir>/deck.json, <dir>/report.json, the answer files in the order written] with subject "morph run <runId>: deck and report" and trailers Morph-Run <runId>, Morph-Cards <deck.cards.length>, Morph-Written, Morph-Failed, Morph-Skipped, Morph-Budget-Exceeded (the number of report.outcomes with that status). → {ok: true, dir, commit: the sha, or null when Commit Paths returned null}. A git failure of the commit (an ignored .morph/ makes git add refuse) → {ok: false, error: "archive <dir> written but not committed: <the Error's message>"}; the files stay on disk.

Steps:
- reads: Deck
- reads: Run Report
- calls: Commit Paths
- produces: Archive Result

1. given a repo on morph/r1; deck {cards: [card a, card b], externalDependsOn: []}; report {runId: "r1", …, outcomes: [a written, b failed]}; runId "r1"; when archived; then {ok: true, dir: ".morph/runs/r1", commit: HEAD}; deck.json reads JSON.stringify([a, b], null, 2) + "\n"; report.json reads JSON.stringify(report, null, 2) + "\n"; the HEAD message is "morph run r1: deck and report\n\nMorph-Run: r1\nMorph-Cards: 2\nMorph-Written: 1\nMorph-Failed: 1\nMorph-Skipped: 0\nMorph-Budget-Exceeded: 0"; the commit lists exactly .morph/runs/r1/deck.json and .morph/runs/r1/report.json
2. given the repo after example 1; the same input again; when archived; then {ok: false, error: "archive .morph/runs/r1 already exists"}; HEAD unchanged; deck.json unchanged

5. given answers [{request: {customId: "../x"}, text: "t"}], runId "r3"; then answers [], runId "r4"; when archived; then {ok: false, error: "invalid answer id: ../x"}, no .morph/runs/r3, HEAD unchanged; then {ok: true, dir: ".morph/runs/r4", commit: HEAD} and no .morph/runs/r4/answers

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response and Stub Answer are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation (P4). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

Callee Commit Paths: Stages exactly the given paths and commits them with a subject and trailers; null when nothing changed.
Behaviour: commitPaths(root, paths, subject, trailers, env): `git add -A -- <paths>`; `git diff --cached --name-only -- <paths>` empty → null, no commit. Else `git commit -q -m <subject> -m <trailer block> -- <paths>`, the trailer block being one "<key>: <value>" line per trailer in the given order joined by "\n" (hooks run; nothing is bypassed), so the message is "<subject>\n\n<trailer lines>". Only the paths are committed: a file staged by hand or modified outside them stays as it was. Then commit = `git rev-parse HEAD` (trimmed) and the diffstat from `git show --numstat --format= <commit>`: files = the number of non-empty lines, insertions and deletions the sums of the first two columns ("-" for a binary file counts 0). Returns Commit Info.

## Function Run Command

`morph run`: processor, deck, hazards, run branch, Run Deck with git's commit hook, archive; one Run Document.

Behaviour: runCommand(root, args, deps, log?), every check before any git call or spend, in order. 1. readRegistry(deps.env); no config with id args.processor → 4 UsageError "processor <id> is not configured", plus ": " and the messages of the registry faults whose key starts with "MORPH_PROCESSOR_<id>_" joined by "; " when there are any. 2. Read Deck File (its failure is the result). 3. Find Hazards errors → 2 RefusalError "deck has <n> hazard error(s): " + each as "<kind> <cards joined by ",">[ <path>]" joined by "; ". 4. start = deps.now() (its only call here); runId = args.runId, or mintRunId(start) = the UTC time of start as "YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS". 5. Open Run Branch(root, runId, deps.env); a refusal → 2 RefusalError, its error. 6. Run Deck, input {root, runId, branch, deck, budget {maxCards: args.maxCards or the card count, maxRetryBatches, deadline: start + deadlineSeconds × 1000}}, deps {config, transport: deps.transport or realTransport(config.timeoutMs), commit: makeCommitHook(root, config.model, deps.env), now: deps.now, env: deps.env, onVariant: keeps each Variant Record and, log given, calls log(variantLine(record))}. 7. Archive Run(root, {runId, deck, report, answers: the records in order}, deps.env). → {code: runExitCode(report, archive), document: {runId, branch, base, report, archive}}. variantLine(r) (exported) = "morph run: <r.request.customId> <verdict> stage <stages>[ <lastStage>] finish <finishReason, or none> chars <text length, or none>\n". A thrown Error propagates to main. The checkout stays on the run branch.

Steps:
- uses: processor
- calls: Read Deck File
- uses: git
- uses: runloop
- produces: Run Document

2. given the same setup, one card a with acceptance "exit 1", maxRetryBatches 0; when run; then code 1; outcome a "failed", reason "acceptance failed"; archive ok with the trailer Morph-Failed: 1; out/a.ts absent
3. given the same setup, processor "nope"; then processor "bad" with MORPH_PROCESSOR_bad_TYPE "x" added to env; when run; then code 4 UsageError "processor nope is not configured"; then "processor bad is not configured: MORPH_PROCESSOR_bad_TYPE must be one of openrouter, stub (got 'x')"; no morph/* branch
4. given the same setup with an untracked notes.txt in the repo; when run; then code 2 RefusalError "dirty tree outside .morph/: notes.txt"; the checkout still main; no archive
5. given a deck of a and b both targeting out/x.ts; when run; then code 2 RefusalError "deck has 1 hazard error(s): write-write a,b out/x.ts"; no morph/* branch
6. given one card a; runId null; deps.now always 1791310149000; when run; then mintRunId(1791310149000) is "20261006-180909"; code 0; runId, report.runId "20261006-180909", branch "morph/20261006-180909"; .morph/runs/20261006-180909/report.json exists
7. given records {request.customId "a.v1", verdict "rejected", stages 4, lastStage "probe", finishReason "stop", text 30 chars}, {request.customId "b.r1.v2", verdict "corrupt", stages 0, lastStage null, finishReason null, text null}; when variantLine; then "morph run: a.v1 rejected stage 4 probe finish stop chars 30\n"; "morph run: b.r1.v2 corrupt stage 0 finish none chars none\n"
8. given example 2 with maxRetryBatches 1, answers a.md and a.r1.md (each a 30-char fenced ts block); a log pushing its texts; when run; then code 1; the log ["morph run: a.v1 rejected stage 0 finish stop chars 30\n", "morph run: a.r1.v1 rejected stage 0 finish stop chars 30\n"]; the archive commit adds exactly deck.json, report.json, answers/a.v1.request.json, a.v1.answer.txt, a.r1.v1.request.json, a.r1.v1.answer.txt under .morph/runs/r1; the a.r1.v1 request's last message holds "<acceptance_output>"; status clean

## Function Main

Dispatch, one document out, the log lines, the exit code; the entry src/cli.ts wires the process.

Behaviour: main(argv, deps, io) → Promise<ExitCode>. Parse Command; a failure → io.stdout( renderDocument(the error document, pretty = argv holds "--pretty")), io.stderr("morph: <message>\n"), return 4. Else root = path.resolve(deps.cwd, command.root); result = Deck Check (deck check), Plan Command (plan) or await Run Command (run, io.stderr its log) inside try/catch, a thrown value → classifyThrown. Then exactly one io.stdout( renderDocument(result.document, command.pretty)), one io.stderr("morph <command name>: exit <code>\n"), return result.code. The entry src/cli.ts (shebang `#!/usr/bin/env node`) builds env from process.env without undefined values and calls main( process.argv.slice(2), {env, now: Date.now, cwd: process.cwd(), transport: null}, {stdout, stderr: process streams' write}), then sets process.exitCode to the result; it never calls process.exit.

- calls: Parse Command
- calls: Deck Check
- calls: Plan Command
- calls: Run Command
- calls: Emit Document
- calls: Classify Error

Callee Parse Command: argv into one Command or a usage error; global --root and --pretty anywhere.
Behaviour: parseCommand(argv) scans argv left to right. A token starting with "--" is a flag: --pretty and --judge take no value; --root, --deck, --processor, --run-id, --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches, --slice-cap-bytes, --spec, --component, --map, --out, --checks take the next token whatever it is; any other flag (also --x=y) → "unknown flag: <t>"; a value flag last → "flag <t> needs a value"; a flag seen twice → "flag <t> given twice", except --component, which repeats and keeps its values in argv order (the first such error in argv order wins). Other tokens are words. The command from the words: none → "no command (commands: deck check, plan, run)"; "run"; "plan"; "deck" "check"; a first word scout, primer, review or report → NotYetError "command <word> is not available yet"; "deck" add|status|reset|clear → NotYetError "command deck <w> is not available yet"; else "unknown command: <words joined by a space>". More words than the command takes → "unexpected argument: <first extra>". Then in order: a flag the command does not take → "flag <f> does not apply to <command>", in argv order (deck check takes --root, --pretty, --deck, --slice-cap-bytes; run --root, --pretty, --deck, --processor, --run-id, --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches; plan --root, --pretty, --spec, --component, --map, --judge, --out, --checks); plan without --spec → "missing --spec", else plan is done: {name: "plan", root, pretty, spec, components ([] when none), map (or null), judge (--judge given), out (or null), checks (a key only when given)}; no --deck → "missing --deck"; run without --processor → "missing --processor"; a run --run-id not matching ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ → "--run-id must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (got '<v>')"; numbers in the order --slice-cap-bytes (deck check), --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches (run): digits only, ≥ 1 ("<f> must be a positive integer (got '<v>')"), --max-retry-batches ≥ 0 ("must be a non-negative integer"). A failure is {ok: false, error: {error: {code: 4, kind: "UsageError" | "NotYetError", message}}}. Defaults: root ".", pretty false, sliceCapBytes 500000, runId null, deadlineSeconds 2400, maxCards null (= the deck's card count), maxRetryBatches 2.

Callee Deck Check: `morph deck check`: generations, hazards and slice weights of a deck file; exit 2 on any error hazard.
Behaviour: deckCheckCommand(root, deckPath, sliceCapBytes): Read Deck File (its failure is the result); weighing = Weigh Slices(deck, root, sliceCapBytes); hazards = Find Hazards(deck) followed by the weighing's hazards; document {deck: deckPath as given, cards: the card count, generations: Layer Generations(deck), errors and warnings: the hazards of severity error / warning counted, hazards, weights: the weighing's weights}, keys in that order; code 2 when errors > 0, else 0.

Callee Plan Command: `morph plan --spec`: the record and the map read under the root, cut by Plan Spec, the deck written to --out; one Plan Document.
Behaviour: planCommand(root, args), in order. The spec path.resolve(root, args.spec) not a regular file → 4 UsageError "spec file not found: <spec as given>"; a map given and not a regular file → 4 UsageError "map file not found: <map as given>". loadContour(the spec's UTF-8 text, args.spec), then loadMap(the map's text, args.map) when a map is given (none → the empty map {version: 1, package: null, language: null, docs: [], groups: [], cards: [], extraCards: []}); an error → 2 DeckError, it. Plan Spec({record, map, spec: args.spec, components: args.components, judge: args.judge, hasFile: a path is a regular file under root}); an error → 2 DeckError, it. With args.checks: Read Plan Checks (a failure is the result); Build Acceptances({cards, checks, profile: resolveProfile(null, map.language), texts}), errors → 2 DeckError "acceptances not built (<n> error|errors):\n" + them joined by "\n"; its cards replace the plan's, but a card the map gives an acceptance (map card by customId ?? id, extra card by customId) stays. Then, args.out not null: the cards written to path.resolve(root, args.out) as JSON.stringify(cards, null, 2) + "\n", parent directories created. → {code: 0, document: {spec, components, cards, generations, externalDependsOn, out: args.out}}. Nothing else is written; nothing on an error.

Callee Run Command: `morph run`: processor, deck, hazards, run branch, Run Deck with git's commit hook, archive; one Run Document.
Behaviour: runCommand(root, args, deps, log?), every check before any git call or spend, in order. 1. readRegistry(deps.env); no config with id args.processor → 4 UsageError "processor <id> is not configured", plus ": " and the messages of the registry faults whose key starts with "MORPH_PROCESSOR_<id>_" joined by "; " when there are any. 2. Read Deck File (its failure is the result). 3. Find Hazards errors → 2 RefusalError "deck has <n> hazard error(s): " + each as "<kind> <cards joined by ",">[ <path>]" joined by "; ". 4. start = deps.now() (its only call here); runId = args.runId, or mintRunId(start) = the UTC time of start as "YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS". 5. Open Run Branch(root, runId, deps.env); a refusal → 2 RefusalError, its error. 6. Run Deck, input {root, runId, branch, deck, budget {maxCards: args.maxCards or the card count, maxRetryBatches, deadline: start + deadlineSeconds × 1000}}, deps {config, transport: deps.transport or realTransport(config.timeoutMs), commit: makeCommitHook(root, config.model, deps.env), now: deps.now, env: deps.env, onVariant: keeps each Variant Record and, log given, calls log(variantLine(record))}. 7. Archive Run(root, {runId, deck, report, answers: the records in order}, deps.env). → {code: runExitCode(report, archive), document: {runId, branch, base, report, archive}}. variantLine(r) (exported) = "morph run: <r.request.customId> <verdict> stage <stages>[ <lastStage>] finish <finishReason, or none> chars <text length, or none>\n". A thrown Error propagates to main. The checkout stays on the run branch.

Callee Emit Document: One JSON document + newline on stdout; --pretty indents by 2.
Behaviour: renderDocument(doc, pretty) = JSON.stringify(doc, null, 2 when pretty) + "\n". errorDocument(code, kind, message) = {error: {code, kind, message}}, keys in that order. main writes exactly one rendered document to stdout per invocation and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.

Callee Classify Error: Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 a card not written; 2 a refusal before spend; 3 a fault under way; 4 a usage error.
Behaviour: classifyThrown(e) → {code: 3, document: errorDocument(3, "RuntimeError", e's message when e is an Error, else String(e))}. runExitCode(report, archive) → 3 when the archive is not ok; else 1 when any outcome's status is not "written"; else 0. Kinds: UsageError and NotYetError (4), DeckError and RefusalError (2), RuntimeError (3).
